keyTerms.definition: One nested layer of the ladder. Shells 0-1 live in items 1-2, shells 2-3 in items 3-6.

recall.question: How do shells map to items, and what checks the depth gate?
recall.answer: Shells 0-1 live in items 1-2, shells 2-3 in items 3-6, shell 4 in item 7, shell 5 in item 8, shell 6 in item 9, shell 7 in item 11, shell 8 in item 10, shell 9 in item 12, shell 10 in item 13(c). Item 13 checks the depth gate.

keyTerms.definition: The wide matmul over the prompt. Weights are read once and reused across T tokens.
The skinny per-token matvec. Weights are read once per token: memory-bound.
Stored keys and values appended each decode step. It buys never recomputing attention over the past.
A taxi rank, not a bus. Finished requests leave and new ones take their slot at the next iteration.
OS-style paging for the cache. Fixed blocks allocated on demand; waste drops under one block per sequence.
A draft model proposes, the target verifies in parallel. Throughput follows the acceptance rate.

recall.question: Why are prefill and decode opposite bottlenecks?
recall.answer: Prefill reuses one weight read across T tokens: compute-bound. Decode reads the weights per token: memory-bound.

recall.question: How does rejection sampling keep speculative decoding exact?
recall.answer: The draft proposes, the target corrects. The acceptance probability exactly compensates the proposal bias, so the output law equals the target law token by token.

recall.question: What do TTFT, TPOT, and p99 each measure?
recall.answer: TTFT measures prefill plus queueing. TPOT measures decode pacing. Means hide the tail; the p99 decides the user experience.
